seo_title: Cost of Living in Baku 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Baku per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The capital of Azerbaijan on the shore of the Caspian: visa-free for 90 days, direct flights from Moscow and widely spoken Russian. A modern centre with a seaside boulevard, mild winters, but windy, and rents higher than the regional average.
pros: Visa-free for 90 days, direct flights from Moscow in 3 hours
Russian is widely spoken in everyday life
A modern seaside centre and a waterfront boulevard
Mild winters, a warm Caspian Sea in summer
Low crime and a friendly attitude towards Russians
cons: Rents are higher than the regional average
Constant winds — Baku is called the 'city of winds'
A modest IT scene and few coworkings
Hot and humid in summer, the air near industrial zones isn't ideal

best_places.name: Icherisheher (Old City)
best_places.description: Fortress walls, the Maiden Tower and narrow streets in the heart of Baku, under UNESCO protection.

best_places.name: Seaside Boulevard
best_places.description: A long Caspian promenade with parks, cafés and a view of the Flame Towers.

best_places.name: Heydar Aliyev Centre
best_places.description: The famous Zaha Hadid building with flowing white forms and exhibitions.

best_places.name: Fountains Square
best_places.description: A pedestrian centre with restaurants, shops and evening life.

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 90 days without a visa — you only need a passport, the stamp is issued at the border.

visa_steps.title: Registration
visa_steps.description: For stays over 15 days, registration at the place of residence is arranged (often done by the landlord or hotel).

visa_steps.title: Renting housing
visa_steps.description: Apartments are rented through agents and platforms; the lease is useful for registration and the bank.

visa_steps.title: Account and card
visa_steps.description: Kapital Bank, PASHA Bank — they open accounts for Russians with a passport, cards with international payments.

visa_steps.title: Residence permit (optional)
visa_steps.description: Through employment, business, study or property — arranged at the State Migration Service.

faq.question: Do Russians need a visa for Baku?
faq.answer: No, visa-free for up to 90 days. For stays over 15 days, registration at the place of residence is arranged.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Baku?
faq.answer: Moderate for the region: cheaper than Moscow, but rents are higher than in Yerevan or Tbilisi. The exact budget is in the calculator above.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Baku?
faq.answer: Azerbaijani is the state language, but Russian is widely understood and used in daily life, especially in the centre.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Baku?
faq.answer: The MIR card is accepted only in limited places; it's more reliable to open a local Visa/Mastercard.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Baku?
faq.answer: Semi-arid subtropical: mild winters, hot summers and strong winds year-round.

faq.question: How do I get to Baku?
faq.answer: There are direct flights from Moscow and a number of Russian cities, with a travel time of around 3 hours.

reviews.text: Baku was a pleasant surprise: a clean modern centre, the sea right there and almost everyone speaks Russian. Rent bites, but it's safe and convenient to fly home.
I moved because of the direct flights and the language — adaptation went easily. The wind is genuinely strong, but you get used to it. There's not much of an IT scene.
